test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 14 Nov, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Pull someone’s leg

options.text: To physically pull the legs of a person
To take a situation seriously or earnestly
To tease or play a joke on someone

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. "To tease or play a joke on someone".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Pull someone’s leg"** means to tease or play a joke on someone by making them believe something that is not true. (किसी को चिढ़ाना या मज़ाक करना)

 
 
• **Example:** I didn’t actually win the lottery; I was just pulling your leg.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct meaning of "Pull someone’s leg" is to tease or play a joke on someone.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

__
 
• **Option 1: To avert a great danger** (एक बड़े खतरे को टालना)

 
 
• **Example:** The quick thinking of the pilot helped avert a great danger during the flight.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: To physically pull the legs of a person** (शाब्दिक रूप से किसी व्यक्ति के पैर खींचना)
 
 
• **Example:** The statement is literal and doesn’t apply to the idiomatic meaning of "pull someone’s leg".
 
 
 
• **Option 3: To take a situation seriously or earnestly** (किसी स्थिति को गंभीरता से लेना)
 
 
• **Example:** You don’t always have to take every joke so seriously.
